title: Person From The Future
paragraphs: “Haah… Seriously, what the hell is going on?”
“Exactly! If you don’t stop this nonsense, I’m going to report you to the king!”
“Once you witness the truth of what’s about to happen, you can report me as much as you like—if you still feel the same way.”
“You said it. Fine, then. I’ll be looking forward to seeing what happens.”
As we were talking, Father started to breathe deeply in his sleep. The town’s lights spilling in through the window faintly illuminated the room.
“Shall I use magic to see in the dark?”
“Where the hell did you learn a spell like that?”
“Probably some ‘because of what’s going to happen next’ nonsense. Let’s just stay quiet.”
So much complaining. Gaining these two’s trust is quite the challenge. Since my magic prevents sound from leaking, we passed the time with idle chatter while we waited.
Eventually… the door clicked open. Completely unaware that we were watching, the crimson swine strolled right in.
“Huh? Isn’t that one of Naofumi-san’s companions?”
“Well, they’re companions, so it’s normal to sleep in the same room, right?”
“But we heard the sound of the lock opening. I saw Naofumi-san put the key on the table when he went to sleep.”
“A separate room from his companion…? Then how did she get in? No, maybe she had a spare key or something?”
“That could be it… but something about this feels off.”

The crimson swine rummaged through Father’s belongings as he slept, taking the pouch of gold, the chainmail on the table, and even the clothes he had been wearing. Ren and Itsuki were staring intently through the peepholes.
“Is this some kind of surprise, like secretly washing his clothes?”
“Then why take the money too? That looks like… theft, no matter how you spin it.”
There’s no defending this, is there?
Kukuku… Yes, crimson swine, go ahead and expose your filthy heart, as repulsive as your appearance.
“Bubu, bubububu…”
Muttering something to herself, the crimson swine left the room. Ren and Itsuki remained frozen in place for a while.
“Did you hear what Naofumi-san’s companion just said?”
“Yeah… That was straight-up… theft.”
“Have you finally understood?”
“I mean, yeah, we just saw Naofumi’s companion stealing, but so what? I do feel bad for him, and I’d like to tell him who the thief is, but…”
Ah, at this stage, it just looks like Father was the victim of a robbery. Their reaction is basically, “He should just file a report.”
Oh? Itsuki looks extremely serious now—his sense of justice is going into overdrive.
“It’s not time to confront her yet.”
“Why not!? That was theft! A crime! We should catch her in the act!”
“That’s impossible. She’s this country’s princess. And tomorrow, Fa—Naofumi will be accused of being a rapist and dragged to the castle.”
“What!?”
“She’s the mastermind. The so-called ‘victim’ is a woman who will cry fake tears and falsely claim she was assaulted. How do you think that will look to people who don’t know the truth?”
Saying those words nearly made me want to puke.
That thing is a woman? No, it’s a pig! Ren has gone silent, deep in thought.
Good. This is progress.
“Motoyasu, is this what you wanted to show us?”
“There’s more. But for that, put on these cloaks and follow me.”
“Got it.”
“But…”

“Itsuki, it looks like something’s happening that we don’t know about, and Motoyasu seems to know what it is. It feels like a joke, but we might as well see it through to the end. It could even be interesting.”
“Even you, Ren? Haah… Fine.”
“So? What happens next?”
“While I’m at the tavern drinking, that pig will show up with the stolen chainmail and try to give it to me as a ‘present.’ When I refuse, she’ll go to Itsuki next and try to give it to him instead.”
“That’s one hell of a setup.”
“Giving away stolen goods… seriously?”
Itsuki was overwhelmed with disgust. But at the same time, he seemed to be half-believing, half-doubting. Somewhere deep down, he still wanted to believe in the country he trusted.
“Hey, then what about the evidence—”

After making Ren and Itsuki put on their robes, I instructed them to sit in the corner of the tavern and have a drink. Meanwhile, I drank openly at the bar as usual. Before long, the crimson swine arrived, pretending it was just a coincidence.
How many times has this happened now? This must be the fourth time or so. Frankly, I’m sick of it. But this is where it all comes to an end.
“Bububububu…”
“Yes, indeed. Ha-ha, yes, yes.”

I simply nodded along, giving half-hearted responses. Pigs are disgusting creatures that can hold a conversation with just this. They think only of themselves and expect nothing but affirmation from others—pathetic, dull-witted, inferior beings. Soon enough, the crimson swine pulled out the stolen chainmail and offered it to me.
“I-Is it really okay for me to have this?”
“Bubububu!”

Suppressing the nausea that came from seeing the pig’s repulsive smile, I reluctantly accepted the chainmail. Satisfied, the crimson swine stood up. If I recall correctly, around this point, she usually mumbles about how she has to leave because of some rule Father supposedly enforces. As if Father would ever do such a thing. Eventually, the crimson swine left. I, too, quietly exited the tavern. Immediately, Ren and Itsuki followed after me.
“I’ve secured the evidence. And at dawn, that pig will come to the inn where I’m staying and try to wake me up.”
“No way… So it was all true…? What the hell is going on?”
“Why is everything happening exactly as you said? Is this some kind of act? A prank? No, but there’s no reason for you to go out of your way to stage all of this just for us.”
Ren followed up on Itsuki’s question. Both of them were completely engrossed, waiting for my response. Finally, I had the chance to explain.
“You may find this hard to believe, but… I came from the future.”

Hearing that, Ren fell deep into thought again, while Itsuki tilted his head slightly in confusion. This is where the real battle begins. Even last time, Father emphasized how crucial it was to get Ren and Itsuki to believe me. Everything I had done up until now was to earn Ren and Itsuki’s trust. At the very least, I had gotten them to the point where they were willing to listen to me. By the way, this plan was originally proposed by Father last time. There were some minor deviations, but overall, I could call it a success.
“It’s a little hard to believe, but…”
“If you doubt me, I can share knowledge of the future I know. For example, in Itsuki’s world, supernatural abilities exist.”
“Why are you saying something so obvious…?”
“Huh!?”
Ren’s face twisted in shock. At this point in time, I was the only one who knew this information. His reaction was only natural.
“Itsuki, let’s confirm something. Is it true that supernatural abilities exist in your world?”
“Y-Yeah…”
“Have you told anyone about that since arriving in this world?”
“No, I haven’t. I mean, it’s such a common fact in my world that there was no reason to mention it.”
“Wait… does that mean supernatural abilities don’t exist in Ren’s world?”
“Yeah, they don’t exist. If anything, supernatural abilities are just a fictional concept in my world.”
“I-I see…”
“Well, I guess if you count things like perfect pitch as a supernatural ability, then maybe… but I doubt that’s what you mean, right?”
“No, most supernatural abilities are innate. Perfect pitch is something you can develop, so it’s different.”
Both Ren and Itsuki’s expressions hardened. A heavy silence followed. Ren was the one who finally broke it.

“Itsuki, Motoyasu must be telling the truth. In the Japan I come from, supernatural abilities don’t exist. The only person who should know that… is you. If you and Motoyasu were from the same world, you wouldn’t have questioned it, and his knowledge wouldn’t seem unusual to you.”
“That’s… true.”

“On top of that, Motoyasu has already mastered portal skills and magic. If what he’s saying about coming from the future is true, it makes sense that he would have them. And somehow, he knew exactly where to find us. It’s a wild story, but everything lines up. Now, about that woman…”

Ren spoke rapidly, almost overwhelming Itsuki with his reasoning. It seemed like he had finally started to believe me. Well, they had already been transported to another world, so I suppose they were already primed to accept something as crazy as me being from the future.
“I can still explain more. Do you still doubt me?”
“Then… Naofumi’s companion—wasn’t she a princess? Why would she do something like that?”

“Their goal is to sow discord among the Heroes. This country views the Shield Hero as a religious enemy because of its history with another nation. So, they turned Naofumi into a criminal to manipulate us into defeating him.”
“Religious enemy!? So they’re trying to make us kill Naofumi!?”

“I see… So to this country, the Sword, Spear, and Bow Heroes are religious deities, while the Shield Hero is a demon. By framing Naofumi for a crime and having us eliminate him, they’re just satisfying their own twisted beliefs.”
“If you think I’m lying, just look at the church’s emblem in the plaza. You’ll only see symbols for the Sword, Spear, and Bow. The Shield is completely absent.”
In a way, they were wearing their motives on their sleeves. Ren and Itsuki must have seen that symbol at least once today.
“Another world, Heroes, conspiracies, and now a time traveler… Things are really starting to get messy.”
Ren gave a small, solemn nod as if he had finally found conviction in my words.
